bodyHtml:
What is inspection management software?

Inspection management software is the system that plans inspections, assigns qualified people and equipment, captures results in a consistent format, routes them for review and approval, and keeps the evidence that the work was done correctly. In the inspection industry, the evidence part matters as much as the scheduling part, because every report will eventually be read by a client QA/QC reviewer, an auditor or an authorized inspector.

The term covers a wide range of products, from checklist apps for facility walk-downs to enterprise maintenance suites. For NDT and inspection work, the useful test is narrower: can the system prove who inspected what, with which procedure revision, with which calibrated instrument, holding which certification, and who reviewed and signed it? If it cannot answer those questions from one record, it is a scheduling tool with a form builder attached, not an inspection management system.

The Atlantis ERP solution is built around that test. It is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies, set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder is an ASNT NDT Level III. This section explains what inspection management software has to cover, how the needs of inspection contractors differ from owner-operators, and what audit readiness looks like in practice.

Inspection management system for contractors vs owner-operators

Contractors and owner-operators both need an inspection management system, but they need it to do different jobs. A contractor needs to run crews profitably and produce defensible reports. An owner-operator needs to receive those reports and the supporting evidence in a form that stands up in their own audits.

ConcernInspection contractor (NDT service company)Owner-operator (refinery, plant, fabricator, shipowner)
Main questionCan we staff, perform, report and bill this job correctly?Was this inspection done by qualified people to the right procedure, and where is the proof?
PeopleTechnician certifications, vision tests, availability, utilisationEvidence that the contractor's technicians were qualified on the day
EquipmentSerial tracking, issue and return, calibration due datesCalibration certificate for the instrument actually used
DocumentsProcedure register with approved revisionsProcedure and revision referenced on each report
OutputReport plus invoiceReport plus supporting certificates, ready for the asset file

The Atlantis ERP is designed from the contractor side, which is exactly why owner-operators benefit: a contractor running it can hand over a report package that already contains what the owner's QA/QC team would otherwise chase by email.

What an inspection contractor needs from an inspection management system

For an NDT or inspection contractor, the system has to cover commercial work, field work and compliance, because all three touch the same job.

  • Commercial: CRM with service line, NDT service type, industry sector and estimated technicians and days; quotations with job type, site, dates and applicable codes, online acceptance and conversion to a sales order; invoicing with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals.
  • Operations: projects with client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope, acceptance criteria, safety induction and work permit fields; team assignments with a planned, dispatched, in field, submitted, closed workflow; timesheets by work type with a billable flag.
  • Reporting: NDT reports in 17 types with an inspector, reviewer and approver workflow and an offline field app.
  • Compliance: certificates, procedures and equipment and calibration.

A contractor that runs these in separate tools spends a lot of office time reconciling them. Running them in one ERP means a technician's cert status, the instrument's calibration status and the procedure revision are all visible from the job itself.

What owner-operators should expect from their contractors' system

Owner-operators rarely want to run their contractors' scheduling, but they do want consistent evidence. When a Gulf Coast refinery, a Midwest power station or a Canadian pipeline operator receives an NDT report, their QA/QC reviewer typically checks the same things every time: the technician's level and method, the procedure and acceptance criteria, the instrument and its calibration, and the signatures.

An Atlantis ERP report records the work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, and procedure and standard references. It carries inspector, reviewer and approver signatures, plus a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature where the job requires one. The overall result is stated explicitly as acceptable, not acceptable, or acceptable with remarks.

For marine and offshore work, the report PDF can merge the classification-society certificate from DNV, ABS, Lloyd's Register, BV, RINA, IRS or ClassNK, the inspector's Level II certificate and the calibration certificate into one document, with a vessel cover page and inspection photos. That is the package a class surveyor or a fleet technical superintendent actually wants.

Owner-operators that manage their own inspection teams, such as in-house QA/QC groups at fabrication shops, can run the same apps internally. The system does not care whether the technicians are employees or contractors; it cares that their certifications and equipment are recorded.

Inspection scheduling and reporting software: one record from plan to report

Inspection scheduling and reporting software should use one record for both jobs, so the report knows who was scheduled and with what equipment. In the Atlantis ERP, the team assignment is that record: it carries site GPS coordinates, mobilisation and demobilisation dates, assigned technicians and assigned equipment serials.

Scheduling rules are built in. The technician availability calendar records assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days, and overlaps are blocked. A technician or an equipment serial number cannot be double-booked. Assigning equipment that is out of calibration raises a warning. Each technician shows utilisation, current assignment and next available date, and schedulers can work in calendar, kanban or list views.

In the field, technicians use the offline app to see jobs assigned to them and equipment issued to them, then capture method-specific data: UT probe calibration tables, RT source, technique and IQI details, MT and PT technique details, PAUT focal laws, MFL scan mode, UT thickness readings by direction, and weld lines with defect type and orientation. Drafts and photos are stored on the device without signal and synced later.

When the report is submitted, it enters review. Once approved, it is output on your versioned company template in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML. The same job then feeds timesheets and the invoice.

QA/QC audit readiness: what auditors ask for and where it lives

Audit readiness means you can answer an auditor's question from the system in minutes, without asking someone to find a folder. Whether the auditor is from your ISO 9001 registrar, a client's supplier quality team, or reviewing your SNT-TC-1A written practice, the questions are predictable.

Auditor questionWhere the answer lives in the Atlantis ERP
Was the technician certified in this method and level on the inspection date?Certificates: scheme, level, method, issue and expiry dates, computed status
Was their eye exam current?Vision tests: near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, expiry
How did they qualify?OJT hours, training hours, examination sheets with general, specific and practical scores
Which procedure revision was used, and who approved it?Report procedure reference; procedure register with approval workflow and revision snapshots
Was the instrument calibrated?Calibration records and certificate register with lab accreditation number and status
Who reviewed and signed the report?Report workflow with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures
Are your company accreditations current?Company certifications with alert days

If you are preparing for a client audit or a registrar visit and want to see these records laid out for your own company, ask for an audit-readiness demo.

Certificates as evidence, not just a list

Technician certification tracking is the part of inspection management software auditors look at first. A list of names and expiry dates is not enough; the auditor wants the scheme, the level, the method, the certifying body and the supporting evidence.

The Atlantis certificates app records scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level from trainee through Level III, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam passed and attachments. Certificate templates per scheme set validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and the minimum OJT and training hours, so a new cert is checked against your written practice.

Status is computed automatically: active, expiring soon at 90 days, expired or revoked, with menus for expiring soon and expired. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before cert or vision-test expiry. Daily email alerts can be configured with your own recipients, look-ahead days and resend interval. The employee NDT profile adds highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which matters for radiography crews.

Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; the ERP simply records certificates your technicians hold under other schemes.

Calibration evidence that follows the instrument

Calibration management software is only useful if the calibration record is tied to the serial number that went to site. In the Atlantis asset management app, every instrument and probe is tracked by serial number, with equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed.

Calibration records capture provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, the result (pass, fail or conditional) and the next due date. The calibration certificate register holds the lab accreditation number, the PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status, with expiry alerts. Purchase records identify calibration labs as a vendor type with an accredited-lab flag, accreditation number and expiry.

Issue and return run through supervisor and manager approval, with condition recorded both ways. The maintenance log records preventive and corrective work, repairs, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacement, with condition before and after. When a job needs to be reconstructed months later, you can see which serial was issued to which technician and what state it was in.

Procedures and document control

Procedures are the third leg of audit readiness. The Atlantis procedure register records document number, revision, method (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, PAUT, LT, AE, hardness, PMI, CR, DR and more), scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria, and either the body text or an uploaded file.

Procedures move through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states. Prepared-by, reviewed-by and approved-by are recorded with dates. Approved revisions are locked, rejections carry a reason, and a snapshot of each revision is kept in the history. Approvers get email notifications and reminders for pending approvals.

An AI-assisted first draft is available for new procedures, falling back to a built-in template. It saves typing, not judgement: a Level III still reviews and approves every procedure before it is published.

Integration via open REST API

Inspection management software rarely lives alone. Contractors already have accounting; owner-operators already have a maintenance system. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. The scope of each integration is agreed per implementation.

Typical patterns include sending approved invoices or financial summaries to an existing accounting package, receiving work orders from a client's maintenance system so the job is created with the client's reference already attached, and returning report status or approved report files when a job closes. The field-device side of the API already handles jobs assigned to a technician, equipment issued to them, report submission and sync.

We would rather integrate than ask you to rip out a finance system that works. If you have a specific system in mind, tell us what you run and what data needs to move.

What inspection management software should not pretend to do

An honest inspection management system is clear about its boundary. The Atlantis ERP manages the inspection work, the people, the equipment, the procedures and the reports. It does not calculate inspection intervals or remaining life, and it does not make integrity engineering decisions; those stay with the owner-operator's integrity team and the tools and methodologies they have chosen.

Where owner-operators want to see inspection results visually, Atlantis Digital Twins presents inspection data on a 3D model with damage and indication mapping and thickness and remaining-life trends, and the Digital Twin Reporting Software ties reports to that view. The engineering assessment is still the owner's.

Atlantis also provides API 510, 570 and 653 inspection services through our inspection services team; that is field service work, separate from what the software calculates.

A checklist for choosing inspection management software

  • Does it hold method-specific data, or only generic form fields?
  • Does it block double-booking and warn about uncalibrated equipment at dispatch?
  • Are certification status and 90-day warnings automatic?
  • Is there an inspector, reviewer and approver workflow with signatures?
  • Does the field app work fully offline?
  • Can it output your clients' report formats?
  • Does the same job record feed timesheets and invoices?
  • Is there an open API for your existing systems?
  • Is it affordable for your crew size, and can it be customized without a rebuild?

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between inspection management software and an inspection management system?

In practice they mean the same thing: software that plans, performs, records and evidences inspections. The word system usually implies the procedures, records and approvals around the software, which the Atlantis ERP also holds.

Is it suitable for inspection contractors and owner-operators?

It is built for inspection contractors and in-house inspection teams. Owner-operators benefit through complete report packages with procedure references, signatures, and certificate and calibration evidence.

Does it handle inspection scheduling and reporting together?

Yes. The team assignment used for scheduling is the same record the field report is written against, and the approved report feeds timesheets and invoicing.

Can it show an auditor that technicians were certified on the inspection date?

Yes. Certificates record issue, expiry and renewal dates with computed status, vision tests and qualification hours, and timesheets warn when a technician's cert is not valid.

Does it integrate with SAP or Maximo?

The open REST API integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Does it calculate inspection intervals?

No. It manages inspection work and evidence. Interval and remaining-life decisions stay with the owner-operator's integrity engineers and their own tools.

How is it priced?

Quote on request, based on the apps and configuration you need. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Request a quote.
